Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Situation2: They oversee multiple teams, resolving conflicts and delays to ensure a critical project meets a strict deadline.
Story: I sat at my desk, blueprints spread out before me, my phone buzzing insistently. As the lead architect, I was deep in the chaos of managing three teams, each with their own issues—one team was behind on their deliverables, another was locked in a heated dispute over design details. The project deadline loomed, and every minute counted. Yet, the phone call was from my granddaughter, eager to share news about her new job. I knew how much it meant to her that I listened, that I celebrated her excitement and offered encouragement. My family expected me to be present, to keep our bond strong through regular calls and messages. But my mind was tangled in construction schedules and client expectations. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in, the urge to be the supportive grandparent clashing with the relentless demands of my profession. My heart ached as I stared at the ringing phone, torn between answering her call and staying focused on the crisis at hand.
